title: Service-level credits and soft-slotting design
content:
Purpose
This doc proposes a "service-level credits" system combined with a "soft-slotting" runtime abstraction for Dedicated capacity. Goal: give tenants predictable burstability while preserving isolation and reducing noisy-neighbor risk. This is an operational + product PRD (sketch) intended for cross-functional review (infra, serving-runtime, SRE, billing).

Context & problem statement
- Customers on Dedicated want predictable reserved throughput but also occasional bursts beyond commitments (marketing spikes, batch jobs, experiments).
- Current hard preemption + static reservations lead to churn, customer confusion, and poor UX when tenants are throttled abruptly.
- Pure overcommit policies (best-effort) harm high-priority tenants.
- Need a policy that: (1) lets tenants consume short bursts, (2) provides clear accounting and billing semantics, (3) allows graceful degradation and evacuation during sustained contention, and (4) integrates with autoscaling.

Success metrics (what we measure)
- Reduction in SEV-level regressions from noisy neighbors by 60% (SRE metric).
- Increase in average burst acceptance rate for qualified tenants to 85% for bursts under 30s.
- Percent of burst tokens billed as "credit-burn" correctly reconciled on billing within 24 hours: 99.5%.
- Customer satisfaction (NPS for Dedicated) improvements on support tickets classified as burst-related within 3 months.

Non-goals
- Not addressing multi-cloud scheduler placement in this iteration.
- Not a full replacement for hard SLA-backed Reserved capacity (those contracts remain the canonical guarantee).

High-level overview of the proposal
1) Service-level credits (SLCs): each tenant receives a monthly allocation of burst credits tied to their commitment tier. Credits are expressed in "slot-seconds" or "vGPU-seconds" equivalent. Credits can be consumed for bursts; when exhausted, tenant falls back to baseline reservation or is subject to soft-preempt policies.

2) Soft-slotting runtime: runtime exposes a logical "soft slot" unit—fractional, ephemeral compute reservations that can be granted opportunistically. Slots have attributes: duration, priority class, model compatibility, and cost multiplier. Soft slots are preemptible but with graceful drain hooks (soft-preempt) to avoid abrupt failures.

3) Credit exchange and backfill: Tenants can optionally fund burst consumption beyond SLCs via on-demand credits (pay-as-you-burst) or via delegated credits from an org-level pool. System also supports backfill of idle reserved slots to opportunistic users under tenant-approved policies.

4) Autoscaler integration: Autoscaler uses short-term signals (burst requests, queue length, token rate) and credit balance to decide whether to scale up reserved capacity vs. allow soft-slot allocation. This prevents repeated cold-start scale-up for transient microbursts.

Detailed behaviors and rules
- Credit accounting
  - Allocation: initial SLC allocation computed from monthly commit, historical 99th percentile token rate, and safety factor.
  - Burn rate: credits burn proportional to vGPU-seconds used by soft slots; configurable model-weight multipliers (e.g., large decoder models = 2x cost).
  - Reconciliation: daily batch job converts credit usage to billing events; UI shows near-real-time credit balance (estimated).

- Soft-slot lifecycle
  - Request flow: incoming request evaluated by policy (latency SLO, tenant priority, model compatibility, credit balance). If reserved capacity available, use reserved. Else if credits >= threshold AND opportunistic pool has capacity, grant soft slot.
  - Soft-preempt: when capacity contention occurs, runtime issues a soft-preempt signal to soft-slot containers/agents. These should: finish in-flight token generation to a configurable cutpoint, flush KV cache if needed, and return a graceful error (HTTP 503 with retry-after + credit-state).
  - Eviction ordering: prefer evicting lowest-priority soft slots globally; consider tenant-level fairness windows to avoid starvation.

- Priority classes
  - HIGH: premium tenants, low-latency SLOs — soft slots granted only if credits > 50% of allocation and opportunistic capacity > 30%.
  - MEDIUM: default for committed tenants — standard credit rules.
  - LOW: test/dev or opt-in cheap-burst lane — higher preempt probability and discounted credit burn rate.

- Autoscaler interaction patterns
  - Short bursts (< 60s, spiky): prefer soft-slot route to avoid expensive scale-ups. Autoscaler only triggers scale-up if sustained beyond a threshold (e.g., > 2 minutes of 95th token-rate).
  - Sustained increased baseline: autoscaler sees credit exhaustion and sustained high queue; trigger planned scale-up and replenish SLC suggestions for customer.
  - Warm pools: prewarmed warm-pool slots can be reserved for tenants who pay stable premiums; warm-pools have lower soft-preempt risk.

API and console changes
- Admin API: endpoints to query credit balance, purchase on-demand credits, configure org pools, and set tenant priority classes.
- Runtime API: returns credit burn estimate per request (headers) and soft-preempt notices for retry guidance.
- Console: per-tenant credit dashboard with projected month-end burn, recent bursts (timestamps, duration, model), and an "apply for extra credit" workflow. Also a telemetry view for SRE showing global opportunistic pool utilization heatmap.

Billing model proposals
1) Monthly allotment + burst tier: base commit includes SLCs; overage charged on vGPU-second price with a multiplier based on priority class.
2) On-demand burst credits: immediate buy; higher per-unit cost but no contract.
3) Org credit pool: purchase large cross-tenant pools at a discount and assign to sub-teams.

Operational concerns & SRE readiness
- Telemetry: add metrics (credit_balance, soft_slot_grants, soft_preempts, per-tenant_burn_rate, opportunistic_pool_utilization). Instrument trace spans for credit-evaluation decision points.
- Runbooks: define steps for persistent contention (e.g., pause low-priority soft-slot allocations, notify affected tenants, escalate to SRE if preempt rate > X%).
- Quota safety: ensure per-host protection to avoid complete eviction of reserved workloads.

Migration and rollout plan
- Phase 0 (alpha, internal): enable SLC accounting with simulated grants; no real preemption—only telemetry and console. Target: infra + serving-runtime internal tenants. (2 weeks)
- Phase 1 (beta, opt-in customers): enable soft-slot grants with permissive soft-preempt behavior and clear warnings. Default to conservative credit burn rates. (6 weeks)
- Phase 2 (general availability): open to all dedicated customers with billing enabled, warm-pool SKU available. (6–8 weeks)

Open questions & unresolved tradeoffs
- Credit unit choice: vGPU-seconds vs. token-weighted units. vGPU-seconds simpler to meter but less fair across model families. Need modeling.
- Fairness window: how long to protect tenants from repeated eviction. 5 minutes? 1 hour? impacts tail latency fairness.
- Soft-preempt semantics: what is the correct graceful cutoff for generation? should be pluggable per model.
- Cost transparency: do we surface precise vGPU-second cost per model to customers or present normalized token-based estimates?

Implementation notes (engineering pointers)
- Runtime hook: add a preemptable slot API that runtime components can check; provide a graceful-shutdown HTTP status + structured JSON for SDKs to interpret.
- Billing pipeline: extend usage table with credit-burn events; add reconciliation job and delta exports to billing systems.
- UI: conservative first pass — show estimated credit balance and delayed reconciliation alerts.

Draft TODOs and immediate next steps
- Simulate three months of historical workloads to compute initial SLC recommendations (owner: Marco, ETA: 2024-12-05).
- Prototype soft-slot allocation decision point in the staging runtime (owner: Ethan, ETA: 2025-01-07).
- Design console credit dashboard mockups (owner: Priya, ETA: 2024-12-20).
- Host cross-team review: infra, SRE, billing, legal for GDPR/billing disclosures (owner: Clara, ETA: 2024-12-12).

Notes to reviewers (informal)
- This is intentionally conservative on preemption UX — we want to avoid surprise outages. Expect follow-ups where we allow "aggressive opportunistic" lanes for internal experiments.
- Please call out obvious attack vectors (e.g., synthetic burst to drain credits) and ideas for rate-limiting or fraud detection.

Meeting notes (11/27 sync)
- Jin: suggested a lower-cost dev lane with 5x preempt probability; agreed to fold into LOW priority class.
- Marco: asked for per-model multipliers; Ethan to mock weight table.
- Priya: emphasized UI must show near-real-time balance or support tickets will spike.

References and related docs
- Related PRDs: slot-based-burst-scheduler-and-latency-fences-prd-proposal.json (see product/dedicated).
- Internal RFC: runtime-soft-preempt-rfc (link in linked_artifacts).

Final thought
This system balances predictability and flexibility: customers keep a clear contractual baseline while getting smoother short-term elasticity. The focus early is on correct accounting and observable behavior; once stable, we can iterate on more aggressive opportunistic economics.

-- Clara
